correctness.rationale: TARGET proof structure (conditional decomposition (1), H3 min->inf, product-to-exponential bounds, Kallenberg identification with C_m=C_*(1-t)^{-3/2}) is verified, but Lemma T proof is invalid: phi(vartheta)=kappa1(vartheta)-vartheta v1 has phi(theta)=phi'(theta)=0 and phi''>0, hence phi(theta0)>0 for theta0!=theta, not <0; E[W_k(theta0)]=exp(k phi(theta0)) grows exponentially and exp(-eta T_n/2) with T_n~n^{1/4} cannot beat it, so Markov step fails. Moreover E[sum_{b>T}(1+b)e^{-theta b}] diverges (~sqrt k), so no L1 tilt argument can work. Hence I3 control for (3) and (6) is unproved and the SDPPP/max-law convergence is not established as written.

originality.rationale: Nearest prior Luo arXiv:2503.05994 states the identical mean-regime SDPPP with same centering m_n, Cox intensity C_m Z^{(1)} and decoration D^{(2)} as Conjecture 1.3, explicitly says it proves only slow/fast regimes and that the mean case was unstudied even in BBM. Full-text theorem-scope inspection confirms Theorems 1.1/1.2 cover fast/slow only. Bovier-Hartung covers two-speed BBM analogues with different objects/centerings, homogeneous Aidekon/Madaule give only inputs. No broader theorem, encoding, database, or mechanical implication covers the mean-regime two-speed BRW limit.

value.rationale: TARGET route: proved mean-regime extremal-process SDPPP would resolve Luo Conjecture 1.3 for natural two-speed BRW with explicit constant (1-t)^{-3/2}, derivative-martingale random shift Z^{(1)} and L2 decoration, motivated before computation and needed for time-inhomogeneous extremes. It is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration, and narrow exact-invariant form is eligible without a new general theorem.
